extracted.intended_audience: Reuters editorial staff (journalists, editors, photographers, video journalists)
extracted.subtask_description: Internal Reuters handbook guidance for journalists and editorial staff on legal, ethical and stylistic standards for news gathering and publication, covering privacy, sourcing, social media, investments/conflicts, internet reporting and treatment of people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy test for publishing images
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether you would feel your privacy was invaded if the image were to be published, and whether you would be able to defend publication on the ground of public interest if we were to publish the image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If publication would invade privacy or cannot be defended as public interest, do not publish. Be extra cautious with images of questionable origin or taken in non-public places (e.g., via telephoto lenses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extra caution for celebrities' images
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrities and well-known people are more likely to bring claims for infringements and have means to litigate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise extra caution when obtaining or publishing images/footage of celebrities; be wary of questionable origin or non-public settings; consider increased legal risk of publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographing and publishing pictures of minors
rubrics_metrics.description: Always be sensitive when you take and publish photographs of children; minors fall into a special category of protected persons and are often incapable of giving legally effective consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even a child's agreement to be photographed may not protect against privacy claims by family/guardians. Seek permission from appropriate authority where necessary and avoid identifying minors in sensitive contexts (e.g., criminal proceedings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish private information only if newsworthy
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether the detail you are reporting adds to the newsworthiness of the story or whether it is gratuitous information of a private nature whose publication is not in the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some jurisdictions prohibit identifying victims of certain crimes (e.g., rape). Distinguish between 'of interest to the public' and 'in the public interest'—salacious gossip may interest the public but not be in the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data protection vs privacy: journalism exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Data protection law protects unauthorized processing of personal data; personal data includes any information that can identify an individual (name, age, address, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a special exemption if compliance is incompatible with journalism purposes — journalists may collect, process and use personal data if required for reporting. Because rules vary widely by country, contact Legal if in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek legal advice when in doubt
rubrics_metrics.description: When unclear about privacy, data protection or other legal issues, contact the Legal Department or the listed duty lawyers; use Lex Editorial email to reach lawyers simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reuters maintains global follow-the-sun legal support; use regional duty lawyers first, then lawyers in other regions if unavailable; for Britain and Asia, external counsel contact options are given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure before reporting on companies with personal investments
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you report on a company in which you or your family has any kind of shareholding or other financial interest you must notify the interest to your manager or bureau chief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full and frank disclosure is expected whenever required by the Code. If in doubt, disclose.

rubrics_metrics.name: No dealing in securities recently reported on
rubrics_metrics.description: You must not deal in securities of any company, or in any other investment, about which you have reported in the previous month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At minimum, avoid trading for 28 days (four calendar weeks) around editorial activity; this is to prevent conflicts where editorial activity could affect security performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialist disclosure obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are regarded as a specialist in a particular area of business or industry you must notify your manager or bureau chief of any financial interest you may have in that area or industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialists should be transparent about interests that could create perceived or real bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment registry requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial staff who report or comment on companies must enter into a secure electronic registry all securities investments (by name, not amount) that they or their immediate family hold, purchase or sell and update entries promptly when changes occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate family includes spouses/domestic partners, dependent children and those over whose investments the journalist has authority. New employees must enter holdings within five business days. Senior editorial managers must also make open disclosure on internal site annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on insider dealing
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters journalists must not engage in or facilitate inside dealing and must remain cognizant of the possibility of inadvertently doing so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of what constitutes inside information and avoid trades or actions that could be construed as insider dealing; consult Financial Regulatory Group for queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest in trading
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists and immediate family must not buy or sell securities of entities about which they have written, commented or reported recently or about which they intend to write, report or comment in the near future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test is whether editorial activity might continue to impact securities. Mutual funds normally allowed but sector-specific funds may raise issues. Enter all holdings in the Registry and consult manager if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advised avoidance of short-term trading
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the guidance cannot prohibit short term trading, it is strongly advised that editorial staff do not engage in short term trading activities of any kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid behaviour that could create appearance of trading on editorial advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer remedies for disclosure breaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there is a concern about a potential or existing conflict, senior editors may instruct unwinding of transactions or reassigning stories; Reuters may in exceptional circumstances bear substantiated transaction costs of mandated unwinding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reuters will not accept responsibility for trading losses; it reserves the right to require affirmative declarations of compliance at any time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid giving personal investment advice
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are not formally regulated then, as a general rule, you must not offer advice to potential individual investors in personal communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not recommend investments to people you know privately (in person, phone, email, IM or other). If asked in public forums (chatrooms, blogs, panels), err on the side of caution and offer non-specific answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial activities should avoid appearing as investment advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing or broadcasting what appears to be a recommendation on an investment risks being deemed 'investment advice' by regulators; the smaller the audience the higher the risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation or truncation error
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a JSON-generation truncation during preparing previous field causing an incomplete guidance fragment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuation: Avoid language that suggests advising customers to take a particular course of action; avoid specific price forecasts; use hedged language and attribute forecasts to others.
